_README: THE PROVENANCE CENSUS — one verdict per file that renders a figure.
Read by scripts/check_provenance_census.mjs, which discovers the sites
itself and fails on anything unregistered, stale, or count-drifted.
THE QUESTION EACH ENTRY ANSWERS: does the payload this file renders
actually carry provenance, and does the reader get the affordance?
HAS_SHOWS     payload carries it, affordance rendered
HAS_MISSING   payload (or its upstream) carries it, affordance NOT
rendered here — remaining work, named
LACKS_SILENT  there is no origin to name, and nothing is claimed
LACKS_SHOWS   an affordance over a payload with nothing behind it.
The gate FAILS on this bucket; it is never a state to
sit in. One was found live on 2026-09-02 and fixed
(CapsuleTier0Preview put the PERIOD LABEL in the field
the card labels Source).
UNAUDITED     nobody opened this file to decide. Capped, so the debt
is visible and cannot grow quietly. Assigning a real
bucket to a file nobody read would be the clean-sweep-
over-no-subject failure this repo keeps catching.
`sites` and `affordances` are MEASURED counts, not intentions. They
drift the moment a figure is added or loses its provenance, and the
gate fails until someone re-states the verdict.

frontend/components/instrument/Amount.ts.why: THE INSTRUMENT. Delegates to ProvenanceAffordance when the payload has substance; falls back to a plain rounding tooltip (no data-provenance, no dotted rule) when it does not.

frontend/components/cfo/BSStatementView..why: Rows carry account_codes; the envelope carries extraction.sheet/method and mapping_version. Item rows get accounts+sheet+method+pack; aggregates get engine-subtotal+method+pack and deliberately NO sheet. KNOWN GAP: rows rendering a <LearnableNumber> (a button) are skipped to avoid nesting interactive elements.

frontend/components/cfo/findings/parts.t.why: FigureCell wraps the cited figure in the affordance, fed by findingProvenance() — source, line_refs as accounts, snapshot_id, period_id.

frontend/components/cfo/findings/Evidenc.why: Passes the finding's own provenance to each cited FigureCell, alongside the dots and the provenance line it already painted.

frontend/components/instrument/shell/cap.why: Money and dimensionless both wear it now. CapsuleFactMeta has no sheet or account, so it names period + tool (method) + snapshot and claims NO source — the mislabel that put periodLabel under Source is fixed.
WAS the LACKS_SHOWS case: `{ source: fact.periodLabel }` on every fact. Now amountProvenanceFor(fact) for both branches, so the sheet and account codes it always had are what the reader sees.
The MONEY branch was bare while its percent sibling carried the affordance; money now wraps NarrativeText in the same one.
Share-of-class is DERIVED, so it shows the row's accounts and period with a method naming the division and its denominator; the balance renders through FactTileValue, which carries its own.
Renders CapsuleFigures.FigureValue, which owns the affordance. Zero here is correct: a second one would be a second card over the same number.

frontend/components/public-companies/Mar.why: MarketFigureProvenance maps cleanly — source+concept, form as method, taxonomy as pack, accession as snapshot, filed as computedAt. Absent provenance renders plain.

frontend/components/cfo/KeyMetricsRow.ts.why: KeyMetricItem now carries `provenance`, built ONCE by the page (lib/headlineProvenance) beside the figure and shared with Simple's twins. The headline Amount wears it; the YoY chip (a delta over a series) never does.

frontend/components/cfo/simple/StoryOver.why: Receives the SAME HeadlineProvenance object as KeyMetricsRow; figureRow threads it into the one <Amount> it renders. Mode parity covers the origin as well as the value. The YoY chip stays plain.

frontend/components/cfo/simple/FirstUplo.why: The three revealed figures wear the same HeadlineProvenance the story dashboard underneath receives — revenue/profit through the mapped pair, cash through its own.

frontend/components/cfo/findings/Thresho.why: LIMIT: threshold.source (the parameter file path) + `rule <rule_id>` as method — no accounts, no period, no snapshot, because a limit is not measured on a balance sheet. OBSERVED: the finding's provenance (source, line_refs, snapshot, period) with `measured by rule <rule_id> · <parameter>` as method. The visible source line stays.

frontend/components/cfo/findings/Finding.why: The Simple headline's obs/lim figures use the same two mappings as ThresholdMeter; the card maps the finding's provenance once (findingProvenance) and passes it to ThresholdMeter (observed) and ImpactRow (both endpoints).

frontend/components/cfo/findings/AllChec.why: LIMIT: threshold.source looked up from the report's own findings by the same (rule, parameter) key check_record builds the row from, plus `rule <id> · profile <id>`; rows whose rule surfaced nowhere name only rule + profile. OBSERVED: `measured by rule <id> · <parameter> · profile <id>`. A check row carries no snapshot or line refs, so none is claimed.

frontend/components/cfo/findings/ImpactR.why: Both endpoints carry the finding's provenance with a method that SAYS it is a projection (`<kind> · projection — <metric> recomputed without this item`, `· fact <name>` when the engine named one). Without the finding's provenance both render plain — the visible Pro method line already names kind and metric.

frontend/components/instrument/shell/Tru.why: difference: `servedFacts.difference() · assets − (equity + liabilities)` — the GATEWAY accessor the receipt reads, not the raw envelope property (the import-boundary gate refuses a label that claims a raw read) — plus extraction.method and the mapping pack (an aggregate over served totals; no sheet, like the BS subtotals). original_difference adds the receipt's content_hash as snapshot; applied_delta adds origin/model/prompt_version as method and applied_at as computedAt. Absent receipt → the two reconciliation rows do not render at all. The sheet's initial focus goes to its title so the first card opens only when a reader tabs to it.

frontend/pages/cfo/FinancialStatements.t.why: Builds HeadlineProvenance once (verified to the cent inside lib/headlineProvenance) and hands the SAME object to KeyMetricsRow, StoryOverview, FirstUploadJourney and, by context, the configurable tiles. Its own figure — the hero score — names assembled_metrics.credit.composite_score when the score IS that field, else the client derivation.

frontend/components/dashboard/MetricCard.why: Reads provenance by concept from FigureProvenanceProvider (lib/figureProvenanceContext) and attaches it ONLY when the resolved value equals the value the page vouched for, to the cent. Headline money/days/count/score values wear it; derived ratios (resolver arithmetic), PercentLevel/CappedMultiple (no provenance prop) and every trend badge (a delta over a series) render plain. The value block lifts above the stretched learn-trigger only when it has something to say.

frontend/pages/cfo/PublicCompanyDashboar.why: The period names its origin: source (the vendor dataset id), normalizer_version as pack, fiscal_period_end as period. Ratios: `derived · computeRatios · <key>` over that feed (x/days/ratio units; PercentLevel has no provenance prop). Valuation tiles: `<source> · market_metrics.<field>` with market.as_of as computedAt. KNOWN GAP: the Overview KPI/Metric/Ratio tiles sit inside LearnableMetricCard (a button) and stay plain — no nested interactive.

frontend/components/comparison/MoneyAmou.why: A transparent wrapper: converts source→display currency and spreads ...rest into <Amount>, so a caller's `provenance` passes through untouched. It holds no payload of its own and must claim nothing.

frontend/components/scenarios/ScenarioCo.why: Scenario deltas are what the reader modelled, not what was read. There is no cell behind a lever the user just dragged, and inventing one would be the worst bucket.

frontend/components/scenarios/Adjustment.why: The lever's own value chip — the number the user is currently typing. Same reason as ScenarioComparison.

frontend/pages/cfo/Settings.tsx.why: The live FX cross-rates readout. Its rate provenance renders as a visible block beside it, which the file's own comment already states; the figure claims nothing.

frontend/components/cfo/products/Categor.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. Category cards are client-side sums over SkuRow {id, category, brand, volume_tons, niv_krn, gm_krn, gm_pct, days_inventory_on_hand, …} — the row payload carries no file, sheet or line anchor, and a sum over rows is in none of them. Nothing claimed.

frontend/pages/cfo/Products.tsx.why: Per-SKU figures in SkuTable (volume, NIV, GM, DIO — card and desktop row) wear `<source_filename> · sku_aggregates` with `engine aggregate over N sales lines` from the row's own line_row_count. Totals, deltas, compare rows, honest-stats counts and the example preview are sums over rendered rows or illustrative data and stay plain; gm_pct renders through PercentLevel (no provenance prop).

frontend/components/cfo/workspace/Worksp.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. The one figure is the financing total rate — base rate + bank spread the user just typed into the form beside it. Nothing was read; nothing is claimed (same reason as AdjustmentEditor).

frontend/components/comparison/KpiVarian.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. VarianceRow carries {actual, budget, lastYear, deltas} and no anchor per line. The ACTUAL column is `buildActualLines(metrics, canon)` over the same canonical headline anchors the dashboard renders — whose origin `lib/headlineProvenance` now builds — but pages/cfo/Variance.tsx (not this lane's file) holds neither that object nor a way to pass it. Deltas are derived (client arithmetic over the two columns). Remaining work, named: Variance.tsx builds HeadlineProvenance for its period and passes `actualOrigin` per line key; this component wears it on the actual figure only. Rendered plain until then — nothing invented.

frontend/components/comparison/VarianceT.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. Same row payload as KpiVarianceStrip. Upstream, the ComparisonDataset the page holds names the uploaded budget file (`label`, `source: upload|demo`, `updatedAt`) — a document-level origin for the BUDGET column only; the LAST-YEAR column may come from that dataset OR from the period picker (F6.1b), and the row cannot tell which, so LY must stay plain until the page disambiguates. Remaining work, named: Variance.tsx passes `budgetOrigin` (label/source/updatedAt) and `actualOrigin` per key; this component wears them on budget and actual cells only. Rendered plain until then.

frontend/components/public-companies/Ben.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. The cohort members carry each snapshot's `row` (source, latestPeriod, lastUpdated), and every statistic is a derivation over them the panel could name — so the payload HAS it. NOT rendered because every MetricAmount call (median, P25/P75, leader, laggard, single-comparable, zero-variance, member sleeve) sits inside BenchmarkTile's <button aria-pressed>: wearing the affordance there nests a focusable span in a control. Remaining work, named: restructure the tile's click target into a stretched sibling button (as MetricCard and CompanyCard do), then wear leader/laggard/member rows' `row.source` and a `derived · median over N members` method on the statistics.

frontend/components/public-companies/Mar.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. The median day change is in no row: it names its derivation and sample size (`derived · median day change over N quoted rows`) and claims no source. KNOWN GAP: the top mover's own change figure sits INSIDE the row's <button> (onSelectTicker) and stays plain — a focusable affordance inside a button nests one interactive element in another.

OPENED 2026-09-03. PublicCompanyFinancialSnapshot carries its own provenance block: `source` (the universe feed — demo | nasdaq | seed_bvb, stated as-is), `latestPeriod`, `lastUpdated`. Price, day change and market cap wear source + lastUpdated (a market figure is as of a day, not a fiscal period); revenue adds latestPeriod as period. The card's click target is a stretched sibling <button>, so the footer lifts above it with pointer events off and only the affordance spans take the pointer back (the MetricCard pattern).

frontend/components/public-companies/Pee.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. The one revenue figure wears the snapshot's source, latestPeriod and lastUpdated. It sits beside — not inside — the row's <button>, so no nesting.

frontend/pages/cfo/BenchmarkReport.tsx.why: DeepPeer rows carry `source` and `fiscal_year`; the two peer money cells wear exactly those, and the leader panel restates the leader row's revenue only when that row is found with the same figure. Headline company values come from the period with no anchor in this payload, and the sector benchmark's source already rides as a visible chip — both plain.

frontend/pages/cfo/ComprehensiveReport.t.why: Every table row reads a served field by name, so the field path is the source (`<upload> · assembled_pl.revenue`, assembled_bs.cash, assembled_cf.delta_inventory; cash-flow rows add `indirect method · approximated` when the envelope says is_approximated). Rows this page ADDS or NEGATES say so in method and name the fields. KNOWN GAP: the nine KPI tiles sit inside LearnableNumber (a button); the ratio tables render through PercentLevel/CappedMultiple (no provenance prop); the valuation envelope is client arithmetic over the reader's multiples. All plain.

frontend/pages/cfo/MultiYearHistory.tsx.why: The extract names its document (filename) and source_site, and its confidence; each year row's five money cells and the employee count wear `<filename> · <site>` with the year as period. No page/table anchor and no extraction method exist in the payload, so none is claimed. KNOWN GAP: the three KPI money tiles sit inside LearnableNumber (a button).
